points.text: The SIR exercise is based on the Election Commission’s constitutional and statutory powers. points.text: Broad Coverage of Caste-Based Discrimination: The regulations de昀椀ne caste-based discrimination as any unfair or biased treatment against Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs), thereby explicitly extending legal protection to OBCs and correcting a major omission in the earlier draft framework.
points.html: Broad Coverage of Caste: Based Discrimination: The regulations de昀椀ne caste-based discrimination as any unfair or biased treatment against Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs), thereby explicitly extending legal protection to OBCs and correcting a major omission in the earlier draft framework.

points.text: Mandatory Equal Opportunity Centres (EOCs): Every higher education institution is required to establish an Equal Opportu - nity Centre (EOC) to promote equity, social inclusion, and equal access, and to address com - plaints related to discrimination on campus.  Each institution must form an Equity Committee under the EOC, chaired by the head of the institution, with mandatory representation from SCs, STs, OBCs, persons with disabilities, and women, ensuring inclusive decision-making.  The Equity Committee is required to meet within 24 hours of receiving a complaint and submit its report within 15 working days , after which the head of the institution must initiate action within 7 days.

Milk Production:  India ranks 1st globally in milk production, with an estimated 247.87 million tonnes for 2024-25, showing a 3.58% increase from the previous year (239.30 million tonnes in 2023-24). The data is based on FAO 2023 rankings.  Per Capita Availability : The availability has risen from 319 g/day in 2014-15 to 485 g/day in 2024-25.  Top 5 states together contribute 54.09% of India’s total milk production. 2. Egg Production:  India ranks 2nd globally in egg production, with an estimated 149.11 billion eggs for 2024-25, showing a 4.44% increase from the previous year.  Per Capita Availability: Eggs have increased from 62 eggs/annum in 2014-15 to 106 eggs/annum in 2024-25.  Commercial poultry contributes 84.49% of the total egg production. 3. About Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Aspect Description About The MPI is a comprehensive measure that goes beyond income to capture the multiple and overlapping deprivations faced by individuals. It complements income-based poverty measures (like the USD 3.00/day threshold) by including non-monetary dimensions of poverty for better policy targeting. Structure 3 Dimensions → 10 Indicators (covering health, education, and living standards). Weighting System - Each dimension has equal weight (1/3 each). - Health (2 indicators) → 1/6 weight each. - Education (2 indicators) → 1/6 weight each. - Standard of Living (6 indicators) → 1/18 weight each. Range MPI values range from 0 to 1 . Higher values indicate greater poverty. Identi昀椀cation of the Poor A person is considered multi- dimensionally poor if their deprivation scores ≥ 33.3% (1/3). topics.title: JAXA Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) & Related Developments

points.text: JAXA Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission on 20 October 2026 aboard H3 Flight No. 10 from Tanegashima Space Center, Japan . It aims to achieve the world’s 昀椀rst sample return from the Martian system. Its planned duration is approximately 昀椀ve years.  Key Highlights
points.html: JAXA Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission on 20 October 2026 aboard H3 Flight No. 10 from Tanegashima Space Center, Japan . It aims to achieve the world’s 昀椀rst sample return from the Martian system. Its planned duration is approximately 昀椀ve years.  Key Highlights

points.text: Mission objectives: Study Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s two moons, and return at least 10 grams of material from Phobos.
points.html: Mission objectives: Study Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s two moons, and return at least 10 grams of material from Phobos.

points.text: Timeline: Arrival at Mars is expected in 2027, and sample delivery to Earth in 2031.
points.html: Timeline: Arrival at Mars is expected in 2027, and sample delivery to Earth in 2031.

points.text: Scientific significance: Determine whether the moons are captured asteroids or debris from a giant impact on Mars , improving understanding of planetary formation and the delivery of water and organic compounds.  Technical Features
points.html: Scientific significance: Determine whether the moons are captured asteroids or debris from a giant impact on Mars , improving understanding of planetary formation and the delivery of water and organic compounds.  Technical Features

points.text: Spacecraft: Three modules—propulsion, exploration and return—use solar panels for electricity and chemical propulsion for manoeuvres.
points.html: Spacecraft: Three modules—propulsion, exploration and return—use solar panels for electricity and chemical propulsion for manoeuvres.

points.text: Orbit: A quasi-satellite orbit around Mars near Phobos supports surface mapping and landing-site selection.
points.html: Orbit: A quasi-satellite orbit around Mars near Phobos supports surface mapping and landing-site selection.

points.text: Instruments: The spacecraft carries 13 mission instruments. TENGOO provides approximately 40 cm imaging resolution ; OROCHI captures images at multiple wavelengths; LIDAR measures surface distance using laser pulses.
points.html: Instruments: The spacecraft carries 13 mission instruments. TENGOO provides approximately 40 cm imaging resolution ; OROCHI captures images at multiple wavelengths; LIDAR measures surface distance using laser pulses.

points.text: Spectrometers: NASA ’s MEGANE (Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma rays and Neutrons) measures gamma rays and neutrons to determine elemental composition. MIRS (MMX InfraRed Spectrometer) operates at 0.9–3.6 micrometres , investigating minerals, water-related substances and organic matter.

points.text: It enhances GPS accuracy and provides integrity information for safer aircraft navigation. Certi昀椀ed to international standards, GAGAN supports satellite- based landing and serves sectors beyond aviation.  Key Elements of GAGAN
points.html: It enhances GPS accuracy and provides integrity information for safer aircraft navigation. Certi昀椀ed to international standards, GAGAN supports satellite- based landing and serves sectors beyond aviation.  Key Elements of GAGAN

points.text: GAGAN operates through an integrated network of ground stations, communication systems, and geostationary satellites. These elements monitor GPS signals in real-time, calculate corrections, and broadcast enhanced navigation information to aircraft. Key Elements No. of Elements Deployed Role Indian Reference Stations (INRES) 15 Continuously monitor GPS signals across the country and detect any errors. A. Recent Astronomical Activities Indian Master Control Centres (INMCC) 2 Process data received from all reference stations, calculate signal corrections, and generate integrity information. Indian Land Uplink Stations (INLUS) 3 Transmit correction and integrity information from the ground to GAGAN satellites. Communication Networks 4 Connect all GAGAN stations and enable secure, real-time transmission of navigation data. Geostationary Satellites with GAGAN Payloads 3 Broadcast corrected navigation signals across the service area.

points.text: Alongside GAGAN, India has developed the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its indigenous regional navigation satellite system. While NavIC provides positioning, navigation and timing services, GAGAN enhances GPS signals to support precise aircraft navigation and landing. To strengthen it s forecasting and early-warning system, the United States made SOLAR-1 operational on June 10, 2026. It is the 昀椀rst U.S. satellite designed exclusively for continuous and operational space-weather observations. The satellite is operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) . Its observations are transmitted to NOAA ’s Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC), which uses them to issue forecasts, watches, warnings and alerts.  Key Highlights

Their protection cannot be done by one country alone because their routes cut across political boundaries. This is why the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS) , also known as the Bonn Convention, is important for global biodiversity governance.

Project Him Sarovar Project Him Sarovar is a new water-security initiative of the Ladakh Administration. It has been designed for Ladakh’s cold desert conditions, where water is a lifeline for agriculture, settlements and livelihoods. The project focuses on scientific snow harvesting , conservation of snowmelt and glacial melt , and creation of small water bodies so that seasonal water, which usually flows away, can be stored and used during lean periods.  Key Highlights
